rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the preceding verse, kayfa is an interrogative of state and leaves the verb of seeing without its object.
rows.anchor: استفهام عن الحالة وهو قد علق فعل النظر عن مفعوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After likening the pagans to past communities, God gives Abraham and his people as an example against ancestral imitation; Abraham is the ancestor they most ought to follow.
rows.anchor: لما ذكرهم الله بالأمم الماضية وشبه حالهم بحالهم ساق لهم أمثالا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause about Abraham is coordinated with the preceding discourse about messengers sent to every town, joining one purpose to another.
rows.anchor: عطف على عموم الكلام السابق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idh is an adverb attached to an omitted verb, with the implied wording wa-udhkur; this construction has many Qur’anic parallels.
rows.anchor: و { إذ } ظرف متعلق بمحذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham’s words explicitly disavow worshipping idols and are addressed to his father and his people.
rows.anchor: قولا صريحا في التبرؤ من عبادة الأصنام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His father is named before the rest of his people to stress that idolatry is rejected even when practiced by a close relative, answering the pagans’ ancestral argument.
rows.anchor: وخص أبو إبراهيم بالذكر قبل ذكر قومه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham and his companions are elsewhere presented as a good model for disavowing a people and their worship, so the pagans should have followed him instead of their idolatrous forebears.
rows.anchor: قد كانت لكم أسوة حسنة في إبراهيم والذين معه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-barāʾ is a verbal noun on the faʿāl pattern and serves as a noun or adjective in the Upper Najd-to-Tihama dialect; Najd speakers say barīʾ.
rows.anchor: والبراء بفتح الباء مصدر بوزن الفعال مثل الظماء والسماع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an is a cause of remembrance because it gives its people honor by which they are remembered.
rows.anchor: القرآن سبب الذكر لأنه يكسب قومه شرفا يذكرون بسببه

rows.speaker: علي وابن عباس
rows.claim: This explanation of dhikr as honor is transmitted from Ali and Ibn Abbas in reports cited by Ibn ʿAdi and Ibn Mardawayh.
rows.anchor: وقد روي هذا التفسير عن علي وابن عباس في رواية ابن عدي وابن مردويه

rows.speaker: القرطبي
rows.claim: Al-Qurtubi explains that the Qur’an honors the Prophet and Quraysh: it came in Quraysh’s language, needed by people of other languages who believed.
rows.anchor: قال القرطبي : ( ونظيره قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas reportedly said that after this verse came down, he answered Quraysh when tribes asked the Prophet who would hold authority after him; al-Kashshaf follows this account.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عطية ( قال ابن عباس كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يعرض نفسه على القبائل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word dhikr allows the favorable sense of renown; praising the Prophet and his people also indirectly censures those who oppose them.
rows.anchor: ففي لفظ { ذكر } محسن التوجيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qawmihi can mean Quraysh, the direct audience, or all Arabs, honored by the Prophet’s people and the Qur’an’s language; this renown has endured, whereas otherwise major peoples would scarcely know the Arabs.
rows.anchor: وقومه هم قريش لأنهم المقصود بالكلام أو جميع العرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is the Qur’an’s seventh commendation in the passage.
rows.anchor: وهذا ثناء سابع على القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question is accountability: believers will be asked how fully they acted on their obligations, while polytheists face rebuke and threat.
rows.anchor: فسؤال المؤمنين عن مقدار العمل بما كلفوا به ، وسؤال المشركين سؤال توبيخ وتهديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to ask represents how widely known and certain a report is; al-Samawʾal (or al-Harithī) and Zayd al-Khayl use similar challenges in poetry.
rows.anchor: الأمر بالسؤال هنا تمثيل لشهرة الخبر وتحققه كما في قول السمؤال أو الحارثي :

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Food and drink are mentioned again because human temperaments universally take pleasure in them; the wording recalls the command to eat of a crop when it bears fruit.
rows.anchor: ووجه تكرير الامتنان بنعيم المأكل والمشرب في الجنة : أن ذلك من النعيم الذي لا تختلف الطباع البشرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One function is to complete the warning begun at 43:65 and developed at 43:66–67, whose detail was interrupted by the promise to believers.
rows.anchor: أحدهما : إتمام التفصيل لما أجمله الوعيد الذي في قوله تعالى : { فويل للذين ظلموا من عذاب يوم أليم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it is a resumptive explanation prompted by the question of what happens to the opposite of the believers just described.
rows.anchor: الموقع الثاني : أنها كالاستئناف البياني يثيره ما يسمع من وصف أحوال المؤمنين المتقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On either account, the sentence has no syntactic position in the larger construction.
rows.anchor: والموقعان سواء في كون الجملة لا محل لها من الإعراب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Opening with inna marks the report as important, stages an eager hearer as uncertain, or alludes to the disbelievers’ denial of its content.
rows.anchor: وافتتاح الخبر ب { إن } للاهتمام به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The criminals are the polytheists who denied the Prophet: the context concerns them, and the angels’ later reply fits those who reject Islam and the Qur’an.
rows.anchor: والمراد بهم هنا : المشركون المكذبون للنبيء صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause is circumstantial with respect to the Hellfire punishment; yufattaru is the doubled form of fatara, used transitively here.
rows.anchor: وجملة { لا يفتر عنهم } في موضع الحال من { عذاب جهنم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The punishment does not let up; no one lessens or calms it for them.
rows.anchor: و { يفتر } مضاعف فتر ، إذا سكن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause about their despair is coordinated with the statement that the criminals remain in Hell’s punishment.
rows.anchor: { وهم فيه مبلسون } عطف على جملة { إن المجرمين في عذاب جهنم خالدون }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAshur defines iblās as despair and humiliation; against al-Zamakhshari, he treats silence as an implication, not part of the word’s definition.
rows.anchor: وزاد الزمخشري في معنى الإبلاس قيد السكوت ولم يذكره غيره

words: وما ظلمناهم ولكن كانوا هم الظالمين
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parenthetical denial of injustice prevents readers from finding the criminals’ endless punishment excessive or pitying their condition.
rows.anchor: جملة معترضة في حكاية أحوال المجرمين قصد منها نفي استعظام ما جوزوا به من الخلود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ẓulm here means aggression: inflicting harm without a lawful or rational warrant.
rows.anchor: والظلم هنا : الاعتداء ، وهو الإصابة بضر بغير موجب مشروع أو معقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s treatment is not injustice because it punishes their aggression against His exclusive divinity and their denial and slander of the Messenger.
rows.anchor: فنفيه عن الله في معاملته إياهم بتلك المعاملة لأنها كانت جزاء على ظلمهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hum is a separating pronoun, not a resumptive subject, since kānū already supplies its antecedent; it reinforces the restriction of wrongdoing to them.
rows.anchor: و { هم } ضمير فصل لا يطلب معادا لأنه لم يجتلب للدلالة على معاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The restriction is already conveyed by the adversative after negation, and hum reinforces it through a second restrictive construction.
rows.anchor: وإذ قد كان حرف الاستدراك بعد النفي كافيا في إفادة القصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most Arabs and grammarians treat the separating pronoun as a particle with no syntactic slot; Basrans call it faṣl and Kufans ʿimād.
rows.anchor: وجمهور العرب يجعلون ضمير الفصل في الكلام غير واقع في موقع إعراب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reciters agree on the accusative al-ẓālimīn as the predicate of kānū.
rows.anchor: واتفق القراء على نصب { الظالمين } على أنه خبر { كانوا }

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود وأبو زيد النحوي
rows.claim: Banu Tamim treat hum as a subject and the following clause as kānū’s predicate; Ibn Masʿud and Abu Zayd are reported reading al-ẓālimūn in the nominative.
rows.anchor: وعلى ذلك قرأ عبد الله بن مسعود وأبو زيد النحوي { ولكن كانوا هم الظالمون }

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sibawayh reports that Ruʾba ibn al-ʿAjjāj used a similar construction with a nominative predicate after huwa.
rows.anchor: وحكى سيبويه أن رؤبة بن العجاج كان يقول : أظن زيدا هو خير منك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their call is either circumstantial from their despair or coordinated with that clause.
rows.anchor: جملة { ونادوا } حال من ضمير { وهم فيه مبلسون } ( الزخرف : 75 )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If circumstantial, their despair follows the call and Malik’s answer; if coordinated, past tense presents a future event as already certain.
rows.anchor: وحكي نداؤهم بصيغة الماضي مع أنه مما سيقع يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Malik is the angel appointed over Hell, whom its inhabitants address to convey their appeal to God as an intercessor.
rows.anchor: و ( مالك ) المنادى اسم الملك الموكل بجهنم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām is an imperative used as supplication; an absent addressee is addressed for conveyance, or a present one is treated as absent to show reverence.
rows.anchor: واللام في { ليقض علينا ربك } لام الأمر بمعنى الدعاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qaḍā means to kill or end life, as in the account of Moses striking a man and ending his life.
rows.anchor: والقضاء بمعنى : الإماتة كقوله : { فوكزه موسى فقضى عليه }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They ask God to end their lives to escape awareness of torment; the answer that they will remain rules out both death and exit, ending any further plea.
rows.anchor: سألوا الله أن يزيل عنهم الحياة ليستريحوا من إحساس العذاب

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿud reportedly recited yā Māl with the kāf omitted by tarḫīm; Ibn ʿAbbas replied that Hell’s inhabitants had more pressing concerns than shortening the name.
rows.anchor: ما روي أن ابن مسعود قرأ ( ونادوا يا مال ) بحذف الكاف على الترخيم

rows.speaker: ابن جني
rows.claim: Al-Kashshaf’s explanation, identified by Ibn al-Jinnī through al-Tībī, is that their weakness and humiliation shorten their speech, making truncation apt.
rows.anchor: وأراد ببعضهم ابن جني فيما ذكره الطيبي أن ابن جني قال

rows.speaker: يعلى بن أمية
rows.claim: In Sahih al-Bukhari, Yaʿla ibn Umayya says he heard the Prophet recite yā Mālik with the kāf on the pulpit.
rows.anchor: وفي ( صحيح البخاري ) عن يعلى بن أمية سمعت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يقرأ على المنبر

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya cites Abu al-Dardaʾ’s report of the shortened form from the Prophet and infers that the Prophet recited both forms.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطية : وقراءة ( ونادوا يا مال ) رواها أبو الدرداء عن النبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only the form with kāf is mutawātir; the shortened form is transmitted singly and therefore is not Qur’an.
rows.anchor: وتواترت قراءة إثبات الكاف وبقيت الأخرى مروية بالآحاد فلم تكن قرآنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥūr is the plural of ḥawrāʾ, a fair-skinned woman; ʿīn is the plural of ʿaynāʾ, a woman with wide eyes.
rows.anchor: والحور : جمع الحوراء ، وهي البيضاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ḥūr ʿīn include women who were their spouses in worldly life and women God creates for Paradise.
rows.anchor: وشمل الحور العين النساء اللاء كن أزواجهن في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They ask for any fruit and it is brought to them; their calling is a kind of command or permission to provide it.
rows.anchor: ومعنى { يدعون فيها بكل فاكهة } أي هم يأمرون بأن تحضر لهم الفاكهة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kull may express great abundance for each person, or comprehensive access to every kind of fruit.
rows.anchor: والدعاء نوع من الأمر أي يأذنون بكل فاكهة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fākiha is what one enjoys for the pleasure of its taste, including fruits and similar foods.
rows.anchor: والفاكهة : ما يتفكه به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yudʿūna is circumstantial from al-muttaqīn, and āminīn is circumstantial from the pronoun in yudʿūna.
rows.anchor: وجملة { يدعون } حال من { المتقين }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their safety is from harm or pain caused by the fruit, unlike excessive worldly eating, or from its running out; it differs from the earlier secure station.
rows.anchor: والمراد هنا أمن خاص غير الذي في قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This added circumstantial clause promises everlasting blessing, since death ends worldly enjoyment; likewise, saying the associators do not die warns of everlasting punishment.
rows.anchor: وجملة { لا يذوقون فيها الموت إلا الموتة الأولى } حال أخرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception affirms the negation by mentioning what seems its opposite: they never taste death at all, as confirmed by calling it the first death.
rows.anchor: والاستثناء في قوله : { إلا الموتة الأولى } من تأكيد الشيء بما يشبه ضده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ūlā means the death that came before, as in the earlier statement that they have only their first death.
rows.anchor: والمراد ب { الأولى } السالفة ، كما تقدم آنفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Protection from Hell is a blessing to recall with gratitude; one should thank God when seeing another in distress or hardship.
rows.anchor: وذلك مما يحمد الله عليه كما ورد أن من آداب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in waqāhum returns to the first-person pronoun in zawwajnāhum by a shift in grammatical person.
rows.anchor: وضمير { وقاهم } عائد إلى ضمير المتكلم في { وزوجناهم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faḍlan is circumstantial to the blessings just mentioned, and the address is to the Prophet.
rows.anchor: و { فضلا } حال من المذكورات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning the Lord where a pronoun such as from Him or from Us was expected honors the Prophet and suggests that their blessing is an honor for his sake.
rows.anchor: وذكر الرب إظهار في مقام الإضمار ومقتضى الظاهر أن يقال : فضلا منه أو منا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement is a conclusion; the demonstrative exalts the blessing’s rank, and the separating pronoun restricts complete success to this blessing.
rows.anchor: وجملة { ذلك هو الفوز العظيم } تذييل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fāʾ presents a summary of the sūra’s aims and their order, returning to the book whose revelation the sūra opened by affirming.
rows.anchor: حيث كان المذكور بعد الفاء فذلكة للسورة ، أي إجمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun refers to the Qur’an, understood from context and identified with the book named at the sūra’s opening.
rows.anchor: وضمير { يسرناه } عائد إلى الكتاب المفهوم من المقام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fāʾ may introduce the restricted assertion that it was made easy by the Prophet’s tongue, or introduce the goal that they remember, with the prior phrase as setup.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون المفرع قوله : { لعلهم يتذكرون } .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Innamā is restriction by reversal: it answers the pagans, who were given an easy path to understanding through eloquence but responded with doubt and mockery.
rows.anchor: والقصر المستفاد من ( إنما ) قصر قلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The object of yassarnāhu is an omitted noun, understood as its comprehension from context.
rows.anchor: فمفعول { يسرناه } مضاف مقدر دل عليه السياق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bāʾ marks cause: the Qur’an was made easy through the Prophet’s Arabic; the possessive honors him, while the language is that of the Arabs, as each messenger speaks his people’s language.
rows.anchor: والباء في { بلسانك } للسببية ، أي بسبب لغتك ، أي العربية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling a language a tongue is a common metaphor: the organ is named for its chief use in speaking.
rows.anchor: وإطلاق اللسان وهو اسم الجارحة المعروفة في الفم على اللغة مجاز شائع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase implies an instruction to keep reminding them through the Qur’an and not tire of their resistance; yassarnāhu means that understanding it was made easy.
rows.anchor: والتقدير : فذكرهم به ولا تسأم لعنادهم فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Laʿalla expresses purpose, meaning the Qur’an was made easy so that they might remember, as in another description of the scripture as Arabic.
rows.anchor: و ( لعل ) مستعملة في التعليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The concise statement teaches that the Qur’an is easy to understand because its purpose is remembrance, echoing the declaration that it was made easy for remembrance.
rows.anchor: وفي هذا الكلام الموجز إخبار بتيسير القرآن للفهم لأن الغرض منه التذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an’s eloquence and delivery through the best of messengers make remembrance a natural result, had the audience not been absorbed in doubt and play.
rows.anchor: وبأن سبب ذلك التيسير كونه بأفصح اللغات وكونه على لسان أفضل الرسل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is told to await the victory he asked for, including famine years like Joseph’s, while his opponents await that and the greater catastrophe.
rows.anchor: فارتقب النصر الذي سألته بأن تعان عليهم بسنين كسنين يوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the opponents people who await their fate is taunting metaphor, since it will inevitably reach them; the parallel wording creates paronomastic matching.
rows.anchor: وإطلاق الارتقاب على حال المعاندين استعارة تهكمية لأن المعنى أنهم لاقون ذلك لا محالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Inna explains why the Prophet should wait: the opponents will inevitably meet the punishment of drought.
rows.anchor: وجملة { إنهم مرتقبون } تعليل للأمر في قوله { فارتقب }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to come is metaphorical for producing evidence, even if the evidence is already in the disputants’ presence.
rows.anchor: والإتيان مستعار للإحضار ولو كان في مجلسهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This refers to a book predating the Qur’an, already present in their minds because it is repeatedly recited to them.
rows.anchor: إلى القرآن لأنه حاضر في أذهان أصحاب المحاجة فإنه يقرأ عليهم معاودة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Requiring an earlier book blocks them from composing a text for the challenge, as they claimed they could produce something like the Qur’an themselves.
rows.anchor: ووجه تخصيص الكتاب بوصف أن يكون من قبل القرآن ليسد عليهم باب المعارضة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Athāra, with fatḥa on the hamza, means a remnant: a report preserved from earlier learned people though not written in a book.
rows.anchor: و { أثارة } بفتح الهمزة : البقية من الشيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Expanding the kinds of admissible evidence makes their inability to supply any of it a more decisive refutation.
rows.anchor: وهذا توسيع عليهم في أنواع الحجة ليكون عجزهم عن الإتيان بشيء من ذلك أقطع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The challenge presses and silences them: they have no proof from reason or transmitted sources, whether written or oral.
rows.anchor: وفي قوله : { إن كنتم صادقين } إلهاب وإفحام لهم بأنهم غير آتين بحجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address to the Prophet interrupts the instructed argument; the ensuing claim that invoked beings oppose people can only be spoken from God’s perspective.
rows.anchor: اعتراض في أثناء تلقين الاحتجاج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Man is interrogative, expressing denial and astonishment: no one is more lost or more astonishing than those who call on beings that do not answer.
rows.anchor: و { من } استفهامية ، والاستفهام إنكار وتعجيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their error is extreme: they reject proofs of oneness, choose inert stones as partners, appeal to gods that cannot hear, see, or answer, then dismiss Qur’anic correction as obvious magic.
rows.anchor: ووجه ذلك أنهم ضلوا عن دلائل الوحدانية وادعوا لله شركاء بلا دليل

words: ستدعون إلى قوم أولى بأس شديد
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passive form leaves the agent unstated because the Muslims’ ruler will call them; a successor’s summons counts as the call of God and His Messenger.
rows.anchor: وأسند { تدعون } إلى المجهول لأن الغرض الأمر بامتثال الداعي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that whoever obeys the Prophet’s command obeys him grounds the link between the Prophet’s commands and those of his successors.
rows.anchor: ومن أطاع أمري فقد أطاعني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Using ilā after daʿā implies movement toward the summoned people, unlike lām in the example of calling someone when needed; the constructions may also alternate figuratively.
rows.anchor: وعدي فعل { ستدعون } بحرف { إلى } لإفادة أنها مضمنة معنى المشي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṭarafa’s line illustrates the lām construction in a call to face a grave matter.
rows.anchor: نحو قولك : دعوت فلانا لما نابني ، قال طرفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people must be Arab polytheists, since the command is to fight until they submit, and such Arabs are not offered jizya; one possibility is Hawazin and Thaqif at Hunayn, after Khaybar, while Mecca’s conquest involved no fighting.
rows.anchor: والقوم أولو البأس الشديد يتعين أنهم قوم من العرب

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير وعكرمة وقتادة
rows.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr, ʿIkrima, and Qatada identify them as Hawazin and Thaqif, fought at Hunayn after Khaybar.
rows.anchor: وهذا مروي عن سعيد بن جبير ، وعكرمة وقتادة

rows.speaker: الزهري ومقاتل
rows.claim: Al-Zuhri and Muqatil identify them as the Arab tribes who apostatized at the beginning of Abu Bakr’s caliphate.
rows.anchor: وعن الزهري ومقاتل : أنهم أهل الردة

rows.speaker: رافع بن خديج
rows.claim: Rafiʿ ibn Khadij says they did not know whom the verse meant until Abu Bakr summoned them to fight Banu Hanifa, whereupon they recognized them.
rows.anchor: وعن رافع بن خديج أنه قال : والله لقد كنا نقرأ هذه الآية

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وعطاء بن أبي رباح وعطاء الخراساني والحسن
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas, ʿAta ibn Abi Rabah, ʿAta al-Khurasani, and al-Hasan identify them as the Persians and Romans.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس وعطاء بن أبي رباح ، وعطاء الخراساني ، والحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause may be circumstantial from the summons or an explicative substitute for its content; aw presents alternative outcomes and entails fighting until submission, with both coordinated clauses circumstantial.
rows.anchor: وجملة { تقاتلونهم أو يسلمون } إما حال من ضمير { تدعون }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naming the speakers as disbelievers rather than using a pronoun marks their utterance as an effect of disbelief and clarifies the earlier pronouns.
rows.anchor: وعبر عنهم بالاسم الظاهر في { فقال الكافرون } دون : فقالوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This points to the situation in which the Prophet calls them to believe in resurrection, which the next verse spells out.
rows.anchor: والإشارة بقولهم { هذا شيء عجيب } إلى ما هو جار في مقام مقالتهم تلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their question expresses astonishment and rejection, meant to make listeners regard resurrection as impossible; they base their wonder on the timing after death and bodily decay.
rows.anchor: والاستفهام مستعمل في التعجيب والإبطال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The questioned predicate is omitted after idhā: the implied question is whether they will return to life after death and reduction to dust, which they consider maximally inconceivable.
rows.anchor: والمستفهم عنه محذوف دل عليه ظرف { أئذا متنا وكنا ترابا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The declarative statement repeats and confirms the question directly, after its meaning was conveyed indirectly by ellipsis; explicit confirmation is clearer.
rows.anchor: وجملة { ذلك رجع بعيد } مؤكدة لجملة { أئذا متنا وكنا ترابا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rujʿ is the verbal noun for returning to life; baʿīd means beyond rational conception, hence impossible.
rows.anchor: والرجع : مصدر رجع ، أي الرجوع إلى الحياة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reply addresses doubts that resurrection is impossible because bodily particles disperse: lack of knowledge of their locations seems to prevent finding and reassembling them, restoring their forms, and returning life; God answers the root doubt by knowing their locations.
rows.anchor: فإن إحالتهم البعث ناشئة عن عدة شبه منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sentence is best read without a conjunction as a fresh rebuttal to their claim that return is impossible; another view makes it the answer to the earlier oath, but either reading rebuts them.
rows.anchor: وفصلت الجملة بدون عطف لأنها ابتداء كلام لرد كلامهم
